land.text: the Fijian islands: 'Ratu Seru Epenisa Cakobau had offered to cede the islands'

predecessors.note: 'On 10 October 1874, Britain began its rule of Fiji'. The kingdom-of-fiji dossier (oc-01) records the cession as its dissolve with counterpart british-colonial-empire; this colony is the state that rules the land.

land.text: 'Fiji became independent on 10 October 1970', with Rotuma 'as part of Fiji'

successors.note: oc-02-b writes Fiji from independence (Dominion of Fiji, 10 October 1970; republic from 1987).

capitals.name: Levuka
capitals.note: Infobox 'Levuka (1874-1877)'; the page's text instead says 'In 1882, the capital was moved from Levuka to the more accessible Suva' (the page disagrees with itself).

capitals.name: Suva
capitals.note: Infobox 'Suva (1877-1970)'; text 1882. The infobox dates are used.

correction.text: the islands Cakobau 'offered to cede' and which 'Britain began its rule of' on 10 October 1874: Fiji without Rotuma

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 82 cells (about 21,000 km2 by the gazetteer); the page gives no area. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Fiji row (1871-1876) is 21,696 km2 (ratio 0.96).

correction.text: Fiji with Rotuma: 'On 13 May 1881, Rotuma was officially ceded to the United Kingdom ... it was governed as part of the Colony of Fiji'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the country Fiji, 83 cells (about 21,000 km2), to independence. Rotuma is 47 km2 (one cell). The Colony page and Rotuma page give no other change of extent.

region.text: the Fijian islands ceded by Cakobau

ledger.note: 1874: Britain takes Fiji (10 October 1874): 'On 10 October 1874, Britain began its rule of Fiji, which lasted until 10 October 1970.' Cakobau 'had offered to cede the islands', an offer 'which the British accepted'; Sir Hercules Robinson, arrived 23 September 1874, was interim governor. The cession is the dissolve of the kingdom-of-fiji dossier.
1877: the seat moves from Levuka to Suva (infobox 'Levuka (1874-1877) Suva (1877-1970)'); the page's text gives 1882.

1881: Rotuma is ceded to Britain and joins the colony: 'On 13 May 1881, Rotuma was officially ceded to the United Kingdom, when the British flag was hoisted by Hugh Romilly'; 'it was governed as part of the Colony of Fiji'. One grid cell.

region.text: the Colony of Fiji as it stood in 1970

ledger.note: 1970: Fiji becomes independent on 10 October 1970 ('With this compromise, Fiji became independent on 10 October 1970'), a Dominion under the Crown (oc-02-b's republic-of-fiji dossier carries it).

certainty.note: An island group: the border is the coast. The Minerva Reefs and Conway Reef (disputed with Tonga) are not on the pages opened and have no grid cell.

sources.title: Colony of Fiji
sources.note: Britain's rule 10 October 1874 to 10 October 1970, capitals Levuka and Suva (1877 infobox; 1882 text), Cakobau's cession offer, governors.

sources.title: Rotuma
sources.note: Rotuma ceded 13 May 1881 and governed as part of the Colony of Fiji; area 47 km2.

notes: Written by oc-02-x. Pages used: Colony of Fiji, Rotuma. The Colony page is silent on the Deed of Cession by name, the area, the Western Pacific High Commission, Banaba, Tonga and the Minerva Reefs, and carries no war: the 1876 'Little War' is not on the page and was not entered. The kingdom-of-fiji dossier (oc-01) ends 1874-10 with counterpart british-colonial-empire; the colonies' predecessor here is kingdom-of-fiji. oc-02-b writes republic-of-fiji from independence; Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire row still draws Fiji to 1970-1995 (oc-02-b notes), the rendering should let this colony carry 1874 to 1970 and end the British row there. Page disagreement: capital moved 1877 (infobox) or 1882 (text).
